page: Google Cloud Platform a3-ultragpu-8g-nolssd is an accelerator-optimized server designed for massive parallel processing workloads. It features 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs from the Hopper architecture, delivering a combined 1123 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with 224 vCPUs (112 physical cores) running at 2.1 GHz, supported by 2952.0 GB of system memory.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core CPU and memory performance. The server achieves a top-tier stress-ng multi-core score of 180184.5 and a Passmark CPU score of 125594.41. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 13946.39 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 431.26 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. In cryptographic and extended instruction tests, the processor ranks in the top tier. For text generation, the system achieves 32.58 tokens per second on a medium 7B LLM model and 2.96 tokens per second on a large 70B model.

A key architectural tradeoff of this server configuration is the complete absence of local NVMe SSD storage, meaning all storage requirements must be handled via network-attached options. This design prioritizes high-density GPU and memory allocation over local disk I/O. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server represents a highly specialized, capital-intensive tier of hardware where the cost is concentrated in the massive GPU memory footprint and high-core-count Intel Xeon CPU.

This server is optimized for large-scale artificial intelligence workloads, including large language model training and inference, deep learning, high-performance computing, and complex simulations like ray tracing. It is also suitable for memory-intensive database operations and high-throughput data processing tasks that can leverage its massive parallel computing capabilities.

It features 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs with a total of 1123 GB of VRAM, paired with 224 vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8581C processor and 2952.0 GB of system memory. The server delivers top-tier performance in multi-core CPU benchmarks, memory bandwidth, and cryptographic operations. A key architectural tradeoff is the absence of local SSD storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions. This configuration is highly cost-efficient for workloads that require massive GPU memory and compute density, such as large language model inference, deep learning training, and complex scientific simulations, rather than local high-speed disk I/O.
